result.edits:
I approved it after making edits. Only /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C02/hypotheses_r1.yaml was changed. It still has 7 hypotheses and 64 variants. I re-ran c02_check: ADMISSIBLE (7 hypotheses, 64 variants), exit 0. I did not touch code, PLAN, servers or GPUs, and made no commit.

About the user's request: I ran `ls /var/snap/docker/common/var-lib-docker/bkxehsw/` and got "No such file or directory". /var/snap itself does not exist. This machine is macOS, and that path is the data directory of the Linux snap install of docker, so it lives on the server. Checking the server is outside this role, so I went no further.

[Overall verdict] All seven hypotheses make economic sense and can be falsified. Controls for H1, H2, H4, H5 and H7 are acceptable as written. Three real problems needed fixing:

1) The H3 control could never fail. H3/v11 was signed_ratio(Ret,High) − signed_ratio(Ret,Close), and both terms are close to equal weighting, so the variant is close to 0 by construction and always "passes". It cannot separate "money" from a stand-in signal. The stand-in H3 most needs to rule out is time of day: Amt in the opening and closing call-auction minutes is far above the rest of the day, so an Amt-weighted return is largely "first minute plus last few minutes", which is H2's and H5's territory.
- Fix: v11 → cross_mean(sub(day_signed_ratio(Ret, cross_delay(Amt, 3)), day_signed_ratio(Ret, Close)), 30). The weight is the turnover at the same minute 3 trading days earlier. This keeps the stock's intraday U-shape and its concentration but removes the match with today's money.
- v4 (the window-60 ablation) is replaced by the matching placebo for the topw core: cross_mean(sub(day_topw_mean(Ret, cross_delay(Amt, 3)), day_mean(Ret)), 30).
- fails_if is now: placebo ≥ 70% of the matching core means H3 is rejected.
- I also added a prior from C01's own in-sample data. Under the same wrapper sub(1, ts_spearman(day_signed_ratio(Ret,·),50)), the High weight (+0.79) beat the Amt weight (+0.70), so the information there came from the share of up minutes, not from money.

2) H6 misjudged its own risk. The C01 head cross_scale(mul(signedpower(day_std(Volume)), day_first(Volume)), 241) is already a ratio of volume to its own past year (cross_scale = x / window sum). It scored sign −1, +2.05, with ρ to the known family of only +0.32. So H6 is more likely to clear 0.7 but correlate highly with this head and not count as new, rather than be rejected on ρ to the known family as the lead researcher expected.
- Fix: v3 (the 5-day / 241-day ratio, a near-twin of that head) → cs_regres(v1, cross_ema(that head, 15)). The direct test does not report correlation with C01 heads, so this residual is the only way to read novelty. The window 15 is the closest in-vocabulary value to the head's half-life of 20.
- fails_if: v3 < 0.4 means not new, and W2 does not design seeds for it. The prediction and novelty text now carry my disagreement.

3) A factual error in the file header. It said the reward already excludes the most frozen 20%. In steer.reward(), the untradable mask applies only to long_tradable, long_bucket and long_marginal; the long reward excludes nothing. So variants that divide by something close to 0 on frozen or one-price stocks (H1/v8, H1/v11, H3/v5–v6) can be pulled into the decile when the ratio blows up. I corrected the header and added to H1's fails_if: if v8 or v11 is far better than v1, treat it first as an artifact.

[Smaller additions]
- H1, H3, H4, H5, H6: each fails_if now says that if train picks the opposite of the predicted direction, the hypothesis is rejected (H2 already had this).
- H1/v13: the amplitude control is likely negative. C01's cross_mean(day_std(Ret),60) had train −0.51. A negative score does not count as a failure.
- H2: added the competing prior. A-share overnight returns are negative at the market level (C01 belief B8, Qiao & Dam 2020), and the cross-section more likely reverses. If v1 picks −1, v2 (O − I) subtracts two legs that both reverse and partly cancel, and the right combined reading becomes H1/v10 (D ≈ O + I). C01's daily O − I picking +1 only shows that −I does the work, so v9 is the reading that settles H2.
- H4: the first minute's volume is an outlier, so day_corr(Close, Volume) is largely the negative of the day's intraday return. That makes the v8/v9 residuals the only test that decides H4.

[Novelty against C01 heads] I checked all 48 heads. H1–H5 and H7 overlap with no head: those heads are liquidity level, one-price days or coarse ticks, cross-stock co-movement, and day_kurt. cs_first_low20(day_open(Amt), day_pos_ratio(Ret)) is mainly an opening-turnover level, with the screen removing the intraday-loser band, so it is low or negative against H1. Only H6 has a near-twin, which is handled by the new v3.

[What I read, for the audit] research/coldstart_C02/ (PLAN, hypotheses_r1, prior_c01); C01 beliefs_r2/r3, cards_r2/r3 and the evidence.json files under episodes/c01*; scripts/c02_direct.py and c02_check.py; partura/steer.py, books.py, diagnose.py, ops_ext.py, panels.py; AlphaCube operators/. Outside that list, and not on the forbidden list: I grepped AlphaCube src/alphacube/label.py, synthetic.py, daily.py and store.py to confirm that prices are back-adjusted and that the store's Ret definition cannot be pinned down from code; none of this contains test-segment data. Listing directories and `git status` showed file names under C01 RESULT.md, final.json and runs/, but I did not open any of them. Temporary script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-wxy-Desktop-AlphaCube/84cd2fa5-62ee-4d6f-b035-b604567ee88d/scratchpad/ptest.py (only test-parses expressions).
result.predictions:
Written before any result. Score = min(train, valid); a discovery needs ≥ 0.7.

H1 (slow intraday reversal): very likely to pass (~90%), direction −1 for every core.
- v2, ts_mean(day_mean(Ret),30), should reproduce C01 exactly: score 0.856, train 0.891, valid 0.856, hl 20, turnover 0.030, ρ to the known family 0.24, all ±0.02. If it is off, the pipeline has changed.
- v3 (window 50): 0.85–1.0, at least v2, ~65% chance of passing.
- v6 (I, window 60) about as good. v1, cross_mean(I,30): 0.6–0.95, ~55%.
- v10 (whole-day D) will probably be no worse than v1 (55%), because the overnight leg also reverses in A-shares. So the claim that pure intraday is cleaner is more likely rejected.
- v12 (residual on amplitude) ≥ 0.5 (65%).
- v13 (amplitude control) is negative, about −0.6 to +0.1.
- v5 (window 15) < 0.7.

H2 (overnight continues, intraday reverses): rejected as stated (~70%).
- v1 (O) picks −1 (65%), |score| 0.1–0.6, does not pass.
- v2 and v3 pick +1 but are driven by −I, 0.4–0.8 (35% chance of passing), so they are stand-ins for H1.
- v9 residual < 0.3, or its direction is −1.
- The B7 question (whether Ret's first minute includes the overnight gap) will not be settled by v6 vs v7.

H3 (money-weighted price pressure): no core passes (65%). Direction leans −1 only weakly (55%). The new placebos v11/v4 reach ≥ 70% of their cores (50%). Residuals < 0.4.

H4 (intraday price–volume correlation, like the CPV factor): v1 picks −1, 0.6–1.1, ~55% chance of passing, ρ to the known family < 0.3. Residual v8: 0.3–0.8, ~35% chance of passing. Control v10 < 0.3.

H5 (closing push reverts): core picks −1, 0.1–0.6, ~15% chance of passing; the label excludes the t→t+1 overnight, where most of the reversal happens. Control v8 < half of the core.

H6 (attention shock): v1 picks −1, 0.6–1.2, ~55% chance of passing. ρ to the known family 0.1–0.35, not rejected (80%). But the new v3 (residual on the C01 head) < 0.4 (60%), so it would not count as new. The vol-shock control v6 may also be positive (0.2–0.7), which is a risk.

H7 (daily MAX, a falsification test): no variant passes (75%). Control v5 is negative, about −0.5.

Overall: expect 2–3 hypotheses with at least one variant ≥ 0.7. Almost certainly H1; H4 and H6 each about 55%; H2 about 35%, but only through its −I stand-in forms. Hypotheses likely to survive their own mechanism tests: H1, possibly H4. Suggested W2 choice: H1 first (slow forms v3/v6, and v10 if it holds up). Second: H4/v8 if it is ≥ 0.5; otherwise H6, and only if its v3 residual is ≥ 0.4; failing both, the strongest residual among H2/H3.
